children: UAE-based developer Fakhruddin Properties has launched Tréppan Vision, a 700 million UAE dirhams ($191 million) mixed-use development that places robotics, artificial intelligence, wellness and sustainability at the centre of everyday life.

Unveiling the project at the International Property Show (IPS 2026) in Dubai, Yousuf Fakhruddin, CEO and Managing Partner of Fakhruddin Properties, said: “The ambition is not to create a building filled with technology for technology’s sake, but to explore a new model of urban living in which technology works quietly in the background to give residents greater convenience, healthier environments and more time.”

Tréppan Vision brings together eight specialised robotic services, AI-native homes, robotic wellness support, adaptable family residences and sustainability systems within one connected mixed-use community.
Located in Dubailand Residence Complex, Tréppan Vision will comprise 463 units across three asset classes: 408 residential apartments, 48 office suites and seven retail units.

The residential mix will include 252 smart studios, 108 one-bedroom residences and 48 two-bedroom residences. Treppan Vision has a starting price of approximately AED660,000 to AED799,000 depending on the floor and type.
Primary lead contractors and main construction packages are yet to be announced but the project is scheduled for completion in the fourth quarter of 2029.

Robotic systems will support multiple aspects of building operations and resident services, creating an interconnected layer of assistance across the community. For example, Smart Care, a robotics-enabled service being developed in partnership with a leading healthcare provider, will bring select healthcare and wellness support closer to residents through robotic systems capable of assisting with basic vital checks, facilitating teleconsultations, delivering medication and conducting wellness rounds.
Additionally, one-bedroom Flexi residences can be reconfigured into two-bedroom layouts, while two-bedroom residences can transform into three-bedroom configurations.
“Instead of families necessarily having to move as their circumstances change, their homes can change with them,” said Fakhruddin.
Inside each residence, AI-enabled automation will connect lighting, climate control, motorised curtains and smart access through a centralised digital ecosystem.

The development will integrate systems addressing water, energy, food and waste, including Fakhruddin Properties’ advanced waste-management model, designed to divert up to 90 percent of building waste away from landfill through on-site segregation and responsible collection. The objective is for only 10 percent of the development’s waste to ultimately reach landfill.
(Reporting by Bhaskar Raj; Editing by Anoop Menon)
